units.cpuMsPerRequest: milliseconds of CPU time (1 core = 1000 ms/s) per request of that type, idle baseline subtracted, includes asynchronous follow-up work
units.latencyMs: client-side end-to-end latency in milliseconds (load generator on the same host)

conditions.cpuLimits: k8s mirror: domain apps/simulation/experiment-config 0.5, gateway 2.4, keycloak 2.0, ECS 2.0; daprd, DBs, redis unlimited
conditions.stack: kotlin (misarch-kotlin main, defects fixed; containers misarch-kotlin-*)
conditions.host: 8 cores, shared machine, quiet windows (see README)

hop.description: GET /health of shipment (Kotlin) at low rate through app only / ECS / own daprd / gateway's daprd -> shipment's daprd -> ECS -> app

latencyIncrementMs.basis: difference of p50 client latencies; the load generator is on the same host

userCreatedFanout.description: publish of Keycloak's user/user/create through the user sidecar: user consumes it, writes the user and publishes user/user/created, which 9 services consume (each 1 delivery; payment also creates 2 payment informations; invoice replicates the user)

loadDependence.description: CPU per request of the JVM/Node/Go/.NET components falls with the request rate (batching/amortisation); Rust services and MongoDB are close to constant. 'rateSweep': isolation demands of 5 types at 3 rates with fit D(rate) = a + b/rate; 'loadCurveCheck': isolation-predicted vs. measured CPU per session under the Gatling mix.

loadCurveCheck.description: per container: CPU per arriving session measured as the slope of the load curve (levels without CPU throttling) vs. predicted from the isolation demands of this file

placeOrder.note: significant CPU outside the synchronous path (steady-state method); asyncTailMs = CPU per request still spent after the last request of the segment (drain phase)
